claim: McpCallerIdentity.sessionId is documented as the only stable per-session key; clientId identifies one HTTP protocol exchange because RpcServer mints it per request.
sanitizedToolkit populates CurrentMcpCaller by reading the mcp-session-id HTTP header at the dispatch boundary and McpServerClient.clientId via serviceOption; empty headers are treated as absent.
GovernedTierGate.runIdOf keys a run as session:${sessionId} when present, else client:${clientId}; a missing CurrentMcpCaller refuses with no-grant-in-scope and writes no ledger row.

Grant sets freeze on a session's first dispatch from session-static composition-root inputs; later dispatches reuse the frozen set; runs are never evicted so grant-expired stays permanent for that session.
Every evaluate seals a write-ahead ExecutionDecisionRecord onto that run's hash chain before returning a verdict; a failed append refuses fail-closed and does not advance run state.
Tests pin that one MCP session with drifting clientIds produces one verified chain (seq 0,1,2 or HTTP seq 0,1), and that keying on clientId would yield lone genesis rows.
No GovernedTierGate test advances the clock past grantTtl to assert grant-expired and non-re-freeze; domain evaluator coverage exists, gate permanence is comment plus never-evict.

Grant contents are identical across sessions (SystemPrincipal Runtime, composition-root operations); the session key partitions the in-memory store, not the grant payload. A new session identifier yields a fresh freeze and a reset TTL.
OntologyChangeActor URNs are minted from clientId, not sessionId, so provenance attribution on HTTP is already per-request; the HTTP test only asserts the URN prefix.

The per-launch desktop bearer authenticates the sidecar process and is not the grant-run key; CORS allowedHeaders and exposedHeaders include mcp-session-id; the sidecar protocol list is stateful-only v2025_06_18.
GovernedEgress freezes once per process/layer, cannot read CurrentMcpCaller, and correlates to session rows by time; acceptance tests assert two independent chains.
Driver MCP servers named by G9 have no GovernedTierGate/CurrentMcpCaller/mcp-session-id grant freeze; session-keyed governance is ontology sidecar + mcp-kit + epistemic/server only.

Shape decision 10 (2026-07-25) defined a run as one MCP session keyed by clientId and rejected per-tools/call runs and an ontology_open_run tool; exploration DECISIONS.md still records the clientId key.

PR 5 corrected decision 10's key to the mcp-session-id header (McpCallerIdentity.sessionId) with stdio falling back to clientId, and replaced eviction with never-evict after an expiry sweep made TTL vacuous.

Architecture files 03-driver-boundaries, 09-errors-across-boundaries, and 12-observability contain no mcp-session-id or session-keyed grant language; the closest doctrine is foundation-mediated TierGate inversion.
McpRequestContext has no sessionId field; 2026-07-28 profile copies optional clientInfo and required clientCapabilities from client _meta.

Stateful HTTP initialize mints mcp-session-id with crypto.randomUUID and unknown ids 404; the stateless admission branch does not consult the header; mcpStatefulRuntime is for revisions before v2026-07-28.
With only McpProtocol.v2026_07_28 configured, initialize is rejected because selectStatefulProtocol finds no stateful adapter; mixed lists allow at most one stateless adapter.

McpServerClient is a legacy initialized-session service; McpServerClientMiddleware dies on protocol version 2026-07-28; sanitizedToolkit therefore yields CurrentMcpCaller None and GovernedTierGate fail-closed-refuses every mutation on a G4-only server.
requestState is an opaque client-echoed MRTR continuation string with no HMAC/verify in Effect source; inputResponses are client-supplied; neither is a session identifier.
Under G4, continuing to key grants on the mcp-session-id header without Effect validation makes the run key client-controlled (new string resets freeze/TTL; a known string joins that chain).

Keeping a stateful protocol on the ontology sidecar, or a mixed stateful+v2026_07_28 list, preserves today's server-minted session machine; both contradict working assumption G4 and are implementable in Effect.
In-repo clients replay mcp-session-id: the ontology HTTP harness and live-mcp-client capture the response header and set it on later requests; missing replay historically 404'd.
beep-effect packages/ and apps/ do not read McpRequestContext today; a G4-compatible identity must be plumbed through mcp-kit before GovernedTierGate can see it.

clientInfo and extra _meta rest keys are client-controlled and unfit as grant-run keys; the per-launch bearer is server-verified but process-wide, so keying on it coarsens a run from conversation to sidecar launch.
